public_rationale: Lovable's September 18, 2025 case study reports that a founder without a coding background launched Plinq, with public-record integrations and over 10,000 users in three months [e1]. Pirxey's March 29, 2026 account describes a noncoder-built travel application that did useful work but developed instability and required professional engineering intervention [e2]. Neither account establishes sustained reliability and maintenance by noncoders beyond very narrow uses, including successful handling of integration failures, so the evidence does not settle the forecast [e1, e2].
limitations: Both sources are company accounts without independent operational verification.
The evidence does not fully document outside engineering assistance or incident histories.
The forecast has no deadline, and the boundaries of 'prime time' and 'very very narrow use cases' are undefined.

our_interpretation: Read as a skeptical forecast about noncoders building and operating dependable software with AI coding tools.
Prime time means sustained use by real users, with ordinary reliability and maintenance demands.
A qualifying counterexample must extend beyond a narrowly bounded utility. Its builders' coding background and any engineering assistance must be documented.
The claim sets no deadline. Present failures cannot establish that noncoders will never succeed.
criteria.support_condition: Broad deployment evidence showing persistent inability to operate dependable applications beyond very narrow uses would support the concern, but cannot conclusively establish this deadline-free negative forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented sustained deployments beyond very narrow uses, built and maintained by noncoders using AI tools, including successful handling of ordinary integration failures.

This challenges a broad reading of Marcus's skepticism, but does not verify reliability, independent maintenance, or the extent of engineering assistance.

evidence.explanation: The provider describes a noncoder-built travel application doing real work, followed by instability and an engineering-led migration. This illustrates Marcus's maintenance concern, but one remediation case cannot settle the general forecast.
